title.en: Practical 4: Measurement of volume of liquids (pipette)

text.en: A 20 ml pipette can deliver exactly 20 ml if you read the meniscus correctly.

The aim is to measure the volume of colourless and coloured liquids with a 20 ml pipette. Materials are the pipette, sample liquids and beakers.
Wash the pipette with water and rinse it with the given liquid. Suck the liquid slowly above the circular mark, close the top with the forefinger, and hold the pipette with the mark at eye level. Release the finger slowly until the lower meniscus touches the mark; the liquid is now exactly 20 ml.
Transfer the liquid into a beaker by removing the finger. Record the name, colour and nature of the meniscus (concave or convex) in a table for each liquid. Always keep your eye level with the mark to avoid parallax error.

problem.en: Write the record for 'Practical 4: Measurement of volume of liquids (pipette)' in three steps.

text.en: Rinse the pipette with the liquid.
Adjust the lower meniscus to the mark at eye level.
Transfer and record the meniscus of each liquid.

prompt.en: A friend says Read the level from above the mark. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Keep the eye level with the mark.
